name: Greece
genZNote: Greece invented democracy, the Olympics, and Western philosophy's opening arguments — basically every 'first' box in a Western civilization course traces back to a small set of city-states here, which is why it's called the cradle of Western civilization.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Geography
bullets: Located in Southeastern Europe on the Balkan Peninsula, with an extraordinarily long coastline and thousands of islands scattered across the Aegean and Ionian Seas.
Predominantly mountainous terrain, including Mount Olympus, mythologically home of the ancient Greek gods and the country's highest peak.
Mediterranean climate with hot, dry summers, making it a major beach and island tourism destination.

sections.heading: 🗣️ People & Culture
bullets: Greek is the official language, with a continuous linguistic and literary tradition stretching back thousands of years to ancient Greek civilization.
The birthplace of Western philosophy (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle), democracy, theatre, and the Olympic Games (first held in ancient Olympia in 776 BCE).
Predominantly Greek Orthodox Christian, with religious tradition deeply woven into national identity and cultural festivals.

sections.heading: 🏛️ Government & Society
bullets: A parliamentary republic with a President as ceremonial head of state and a Prime Minister as head of government, established after the monarchy was abolished by referendum in 1974.
Widely credited as the birthplace of democracy, with ancient Athens' direct democratic assembly seen as a foundational model for modern representative government.
Experienced a severe sovereign debt crisis (2009-2018) that led to major EU/IMF bailout programmes and significant economic austerity measures.

sections.heading: 🧬 Medical & Scientific Developments
bullets: Historic birthplace of Western medicine through Hippocrates, whose ethical principles still underpin the modern medical 'Hippocratic Oath'.
Ancient Greek scholars made foundational contributions to mathematics (Euclid, Pythagoras) and astronomy (Ptolemy, Aristarchus).
A significant modern shipping and maritime engineering industry, with Greek-owned vessels forming one of the largest merchant shipping fleets in the world.

sections.heading: 🌐 Global Relations
bullets: A European Union and NATO member, and the modern host and origin of the Olympic Games tradition, including hosting the 2004 Athens Olympics.
Has a long-standing, complex relationship with neighbouring Turkey, including disputes over Aegean Sea territorial boundaries and Cyprus.
Plays a strategically significant role for the EU and NATO given its location bordering the Balkans, Turkey, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

sections.heading: 🇮🇳 Relations with India
bullets: India and Greece elevated relations to a 'Strategic Partnership' in 2023, with growing defence, shipping, and infrastructure cooperation.
Both countries share ancient civilizational depth, with historic contact dating to Alexander the Great's campaigns into northwestern India (326 BCE), a notable shared historical reference point.
Greek shipping expertise and India's shipbuilding ambitions offer growing areas of maritime cooperation.

sections.heading: 📦 Trade & Economy
bullets: A services-driven economy heavily reliant on tourism and shipping, alongside agriculture (olives, olive oil, wine).
Owns one of the world's largest merchant shipping fleets by tonnage, a historically significant national industry.
Recovering steadily from its 2009-2018 sovereign debt crisis, with tourism remaining the primary growth driver.

sections.heading: ⭐ What It's Known For
bullets: Being the birthplace of democracy, philosophy, and the Olympic Games.
Ancient monuments including the Parthenon and Acropolis in Athens.
Owning one of the world's largest merchant shipping fleets.
Thousands of scenic Aegean and Ionian islands as major tourism destinations.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Greece is a Southeastern European parliamentary republic, the historic birthplace of democracy and philosophy, an EU/NATO member and major global shipping power.
keyFacts: Parliamentary republic since the monarchy's abolition by referendum in 1974.
Birthplace of democracy, philosophy (Socrates, Plato, Aristotle), and the Olympic Games.
Owns one of the world's largest merchant shipping fleets.
commonConfusion: Ancient Greek civilization (city-states like Athens and Sparta) predates the modern Greek nation-state by over two millennia — they are historically continuous but politically distinct.

highYieldFacts: Greece: parliamentary republic since 1974; birthplace of democracy and the Olympics.
EU/NATO member; one of the world's largest merchant shipping fleets.
India-Greece: Strategic Partnership since 2023; historic link via Alexander the Great's 326 BCE campaign into India.
commonTraps: Assuming modern Greece has been a continuous single political state since antiquity — it emerged as a modern nation only in the 19th century.
Confusing Greece's sovereign debt crisis (2009-2018) with its ancient historical legacy.
mustRemember: Greece: democracy's birthplace, EU/NATO member, global shipping power, Strategic Partner with India since 2023.
